items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: then I played with Tiny about six months in the club there.

ctx.x: In Lips' band? I don't remember. I really don't remember but he had a good band. Sandy was on that band. It was a good little band he had. And then I worked in 52nd Street with Tiny Grimes had a little band. And

then I played with Tiny about six months in the club there. And Billie Holiday was singing in the club. We backed her, in fact. And the other act in there was Art Tatum. That's -- those were the two acts in that club. That was also the Yacht Club on 52nd, Club. It was right across the street from the Onyx Club. Yeah.

And I had a ball playing for her. I couldn't get out of the room because Art Tatum was coming on after her, you know. I just went to the john and that was about it, man, and I came back on. Yeah, it was a lot of fun. And Tiny had a good little band. John Hardee -- I don't know if you ever knew him -- a tenor man was playing tenor, myself, and Curly Russell was on bass, and Marlowe Morris was on piano, and the drummer Harold was West -- Eddie West -- not Harold West -- Eddie West, I think, was the drummer from…

items.title: 67425_Tiny Grimes oral history interview
items.q: And Trumpy Young used to come around and play.

ctx.x: Yeah, Because my name was pretty warm then, just after I left Tatum. So I say yeah, I get a band. We couldn't get nothin' but a little over scale, you know, but a least it was a start for me to get that type of thing started. I had the right guys, you know, fellas could play good, and they knew the type of thing I played, so that's how that started. With 4 pieces, just the rhythm section, no horn. Horns came in later. And John Hardee was in the Army, and he started coming around... And Trumpy Young used to come…
